desc: Every year since 1995 the President of the United States has personally signed a determination, published in the Federal Register, exempting 'the Air Force's Operating Location Near Groom Lake, Nevada' from the disclosure requirements of federal environmental law in the interest of national security. The document is remarkable for what it does not do: it never names the facility, never describes what is there, and never explains what disclosure would reveal. It exists because workers alleged they had been made ill by the open-air burning of classified waste and sued, and because the government elected to shield the facility rather than litigate the facts. The Ninth Circuit sustained that position in Kasza v. Browner, 133 F.3d 1159 (1998), and the Supreme Court denied certiorari at 525 U.S. 967. The determinations are the cleanest documentary proof on this board that the United States maintains a contractor-operated facility whose contents are exempted from statutory disclosure by annual presidential action - the legal envelope inside which anything at all can be held.

timeline.text: Kasza v. Browner, 133 F.3d 1159, sustains dismissal on state secrets and statutory exemption grounds. The Supreme Court denies certiorari at 525 U.S. 967. The facility's contents remain legally unspeakable.
